subject: Intermittent large-packet drops during private cutover — asymmetric NAT & SG policy suspect
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morton <alice.morton@brightleaf.com>, netops@brightleaf.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent large-packet drops during private cutover — first report

Hi Alice / BrightLeaf NetOps team,

We started the private cutover to your VPC this morning (cutover window 09:00–11:00 PDT). During the first phase of traffic shift we observed repeated application-layer failures from a subset of hosts: large POST payloads (5–20KB) are failing intermittently with TCP retransmits and client timeouts.

What we've captured so far: 
- Edge health checks to the application tier show ~0.5–3% packet loss for large TCP transfers during the shift; small packets unaffected.
- Our edge logs show SYN/ACKs being sent but subsequent payload segments are not acknowledged.
- Initial pcap attached (pcap_edge_drop.pcap) and traceroute/path capture (path-trace-aug16.txt).

Hypothesis so far: packet MTU / MSS issues + asymmetric return path (SNAT on one leg) causing large-segment drops or firewall state mismatch. I'm CC'ing Markus and Dev from Networking to assist. Can you share your gateway/router MTU, any inline firewall or load-balancer MSS clamping, and whether BrightLeaf is performing ephemeral SNAT for return traffic?

Requested next steps: 
1) Please attach your traceroute + tcpdump from the app subnet for the same time window.
2) If you have an edge firewall, confirm if it drops packets above X size or modifies MSS.
3) If possible, hold cutover traffic to the affected subnets while we coordinate a short test (we can do a controlled RST/blocked test and then re-enable).

Thanks — we want to avoid a rollback if we can patch quickly.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: pcap_edge_drop.pcap (pcap summary stub)
Attachment: path-trace-aug16.txt (hops + timestamps)

From: Alice Morton <alice.morton@brightleaf.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: netops@brightleaf.com, support@brightleaf.com
Date: 2025-08-16T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drops during private cutover — first report

Marissa — thanks for the quick heads up. We saw the same client errors and paused phase 2 of the cutover at 09:45.

Preliminary info from our side: 
- Our DirectConnect uplink MTU is 9000 on our side; the customer gateway in the colo is set to 1500 for the transit VLAN.
- We do have an inline firewall (vendor appliance) performing stateful inspection. We do not actively rewrite MSS, but we have an older firmware that historically had issues with segmented large packets under high connection churn.
- For the cutover we are applying SNAT on the transit edge for some legacy on-prem resources; new VPC subnets should be using 1:1 routing but a subset still hit the SNAT path.

I've attached our packet trace for the app subnet (brightleaf-trace-aug16.txt). You can see the skewed hop counts and a few retransmits matching your timestamps.

We can: 
- Open a maintenance window at 2025-08-17 01:00–02:00 UTC to run an isolated test where we temporarily disable SNAT on the transit appliance for the affected prefixes.
- Provide firewall logs for the time window.

If you think SG policy on your side could be causing retransmits (blocks on fragmented packets) let us know the exact test steps and we'll coordinate.

— Alice
Alice Morton
Cloud Network Lead, BrightLeaf Inc.

---
Attachment: brightleaf-trace-aug16.txt

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, Alice Morton <alice.morton@brightleaf.com>
Date: 2025-08-16T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drops during private cutover — hypothesis and short test plan

Looping in Laura for escalation/context. Quick notes from infra: 

Findings from our edge and gateway logs: 
- We see pairs of flows where initial SYN/SYN-ACK complete, but payload segments (length > 1400 bytes) are not ACKed.
- Conntrack shows NAT translation established but short-lived entries for some return directions (ephemeral port reuse TTL ~30s).
- Security group rules on our side allow all established traffic; we do not intentionally drop fragments. However, our VPC egress SG does not explicitly allow 'fragmented packets' flags — some older firewall implementations can treat fragments as invalid if SGs are strict.

Quick test proposals (pick one):
A) Temporarily disable SNAT on BrightLeaf transit for one affected prefix and run synthetic large-payload POSTs for 15 minutes.
B) If SNAT change is not possible, we add an intermediate MTU clamp on our edge (tcp_mss clamp on the load balancer) to force segment sizes < 1400 and re-run the cutover.

I'll prepare iptables/tcpproxy rules we can push as a short-lived canary. If we need to escalate to firmware vendor (firewall), we'll need packet captures with timestamps.

-- Markus
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Morton <alice.morton@brightleaf.com>, netops@brightleaf.com
Date: 2025-08-17T02:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drops during private cutover — fw evidence + mitigation steps

Quick follow-up after running a short canary in our staging slice overnight (results attached).

What we found: 
- The firewall in the transit path is dropping fragments when the SYN cookie / conntrack entry is briefly missing (fw-syn-retry.log shows repeated "SYN_RETRY" and fragment discard events at the firewall).
- Asymmetric route observed: return traffic for some subnets is taking an alternate colo path that performs SNAT at the edge; reverse path uses a different ASM causing lack of state on the inspection device.
- MSS/MTU mismatch: our edge MTU is 9000 internally but the transit VLAN enforces 1500. Payload segmentation without MSS clamp leads to fragments that the older firewall drops.

Immediate mitigation we applied in staging for validation: 
1) Applied iptables rule to clamp TCP MSS to 1360 on the LB instances (prevents fragmentation).
2) Added an ip rule to ensure symmetric SNAT mapping for the short test (forces return via same next-hop).
3) Kept conntrack timeouts increased to 180s for this prefix to reduce early expiry on high churn.

After these changes we re-ran the POST test (10k calls) — failure rate dropped to <0.1%. Logs and the fw-syn-retry.log are attached.

Proposed production plan for the maintenance window (2025-08-17 01:00–02:00 UTC as suggested): 
- At T0: push MSS clamp on LB (rollback script prepared).
- At T+10m: coordinate BrightLeaf to disable SNAT for the test prefix (if possible).
- Run 15-minute synthetic load.
- If green, remove temporary conntrack extend and schedule a config follow-up to either update firewall firmware or enforce MSS clamping in routing fabric.

I'll own rollout and rollback scripts. Markus / Laura — please review the commands in the shared drive link and confirm.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: fw-syn-retry.log

Subject: Re: Intermittent large-packet drops during private cutover — next steps and maintenance window confirmed

Team — appreciate the detailed investigation and the staging results. We can proceed with the planned maintenance window. Confirmations: 
- SNAT will be temporarily disabled for the test prefix at 2025-08-17 01:10:00 UTC (we have ticketed the change and will snapshot the appliance).
- BrightLeaf will monitor fw logs and share them in real time.
- After the test, if success, we will schedule firmware upgrade with our vendor and keep the MSS clamp as a long-term mitigation until the firmware is validated.

Please post the exact CLI snippets you will push and the rollback plan to the Drive link so our on-call can apply them. Also add a short rollback playbook in the Jira ticket JIRA-INC-2731.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Morton
Cloud Network Lead, BrightLeaf Inc.
